intent: Bring setup_night_lockdown.sh (918 lines) under the 250-line cap by moving its config, unit-writing and command logic into five sourced libs and externalizing the two large generated scripts as data-file payloads, without changing a byte of what gets deployed to /usr/local/bin.
scope: New libs: lib/nl_commands.sh (82), lib/nl_config.sh (125), lib/nl_enter.sh (12), lib/nl_units.sh (100), lib/nl_unlock.sh (12)
Non-goal: running setup or unlock, which write /etc/systemd/system and /usr/local/bin and reconfigure this machine's night lockdown
Non-goal: shell test coverage; no suite exists for this script
changes: Split into five libs by responsibility: nl_config (configuration file and derived values), nl_units (systemd unit and timer generation), nl_commands (the setup/status/unlock subcommands), nl_enter and nl_unlock (installing the two generated scripts).

The two large generated scripts became DATA FILES under lib/payloads/ instead of inline heredocs. ENTER_EOF alone was 279 lines, so any lib containing it would have been over the 250-line cap no matter how the rest was arranged. Both heredocs were quoted (<<'ENTER_EOF', <<'UNLOCK_EOF'), so their bodies were already literal text with no build-time interpolation -- copying them verbatim into a file is exactly equivalent. Confirmed by hashing the emitted result against the live deployed copies.

The payloads are named *.sh.in rather than *.sh, deliberately. The pre-commit hook globs staged files with '\.(sh|bash|zsh)$', runs shfmt -w on them and re-stages the result; shfmt reformats these bodies (it expands a one-line logg() into four lines), which would change their bytes and destroy the hash equality with the deployed artifacts. The .in extension keeps them out of every .sh-globbing hook. No suppression or exclude regex was added.
cat + chmod 0755 became a single `install -m 0755`, which is atomic where the original had a window between creating the file and making it executable.

verification.evidence: Over-cap list went from 3 files to 2; setup_night_lockdown.sh no longer listed. Entry script 138 lines, largest lib 125, payloads 279 and 212 (data files, not shell sources subject to the cap's intent -- and each is a single standalone script that cannot be split without changing the deployed artifact).

verification.command: diff of `help`, `status` and an unknown command against pre-split baselines
verification.evidence: All three byte-identical with unchanged exit codes 0/0/1. `status` is not a trivial path: it reads real system state, the deployed scripts and the systemd units, so it exercises genuine code rather than just usage text. Re-verified after shfmt.

verification.command: sha256 of the EMITTED artifacts vs the live deployed /usr/local/bin copies
verification.evidence: THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK. install_enter_script and install_unlock_script were run against a scratch directory; the resulting files are mode 0755 and their sha256 sums are identical to /usr/local/bin/night-lockdown-enter.sh (4baaf405...) and night-lockdown-unlock.sh (eafce28d...). Re-run after the .sh.in rename and still identical. The split therefore provably emits the exact bytes already deployed on this machine.

verification.command: python3 line-multiset check of entry + 5 libs + 2 payloads against HEAD's 918-line file
verification.evidence: Exactly 6 functional lines differ, all explained by the heredoc-to-data-file conversion: the two `cat >... <<'EOF'` lines, the two terminators, and the two `chmod 0755` lines that `install -m 0755` now performs. Nothing else was lost.

verification.command: sha256sum -c on the deployed artifacts, before and after the whole change
verification.evidence: Both /usr/local/bin scripts report OK. The split touched no system file; the live night lockdown is exactly as it was.

verification.command: shellcheck (no -x) + shfmt idempotence + bash -n on the entry script and five libs
verification.evidence: shellcheck rc=0 with no suppressions; shfmt -w is a no-op on all six after formatting the entry script by hand, so the pre-commit auto-format cannot alter them; all parse.

risks: The .sh.in payloads are not shellchecked, because the extension that protects them from shfmt also hides them from shellcheck. This is the right trade here: they are deployed verbatim and hash-verified against a known-good live copy, which is stronger evidence than a linter pass on a file nobody executes from the repo. They were shellcheck-clean as .sh before the rename.

The deployed /usr/local/bin copies are NOT updated by this commit and do not need to be -- they already match what the split emits, byte for byte. Re-running `setup` would rewrite them with identical content.

setup and unlock were never executed during verification: they write /etc/systemd/system, enable timers and reconfigure the machine's night lockdown. Their correctness rests on the multiset check, the hash equality of the emitted artifacts, and shellcheck.
rollback: git revert this commit; setup_night_lockdown.sh returns to a single 918-line file and lib/nl_*.sh plus lib/payloads/ disappear.
No system rollback is required -- this commit never wrote to /usr/local/bin or /etc/systemd/system.
Validate with: bash setup_night_lockdown.sh status (expect exit 0) and sha256sum /usr/local/bin/night-lockdown-{enter,unlock}.sh (expect 4baaf405... and eafce28d...).
